mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth prospects diminish.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of quarters with negative GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index by more than 0.5% in a month signals deflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPI decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and housing starts also increase by more than 5% in the same month, it signals a strong demand environment, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and consumer confidence rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and HOUST increases > 5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between PAYEMS/HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% and remains there for three consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as wage pressures and consumer spending increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between low UNRATE and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of months with positive RSAFS growth, or the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
